messages:
mike: quick heads-up — seeing a ~12% p95 token latency regression after turning on speculative decoding for Mixtral when paired with Llama drafts. profiler shows a spike in kernel switches and more frequent kv reallocs. logs: `kernel_switches: 312 -> 780`, `avg_kernel_launch_ms: 0.12 -> 0.36`

anna: can you paste the pairing config and batch settings? also: is KV warmed or are we invalidating prefixes a lot?

mike: here's the canary config i used:
```
batching: {max_batch_tokens: 4096, max_concurrent: 64}
draft_pair: {primary: mixtral-8x, draft: llama-2-13b, speculative: true}
speculative: {acceptance_rate: 0.25, timeout_ms: 45}
kv: {layout: auto, cache_warm: true}
```
KV hit-rate was ~0.92 overall but the tracer shows periodic full-kv re-allocs when ropescale mismatch happens (see profiler trace id: trace-1769998888).

sara: flamegraph looked like kernel churn attached to attention kernel selection logic. my hunch: mismatch in head/kv dims + rotary scaling leads to taking a different code path (fallback to generic kernel) for certain seq-lens. quick check: `python -c "print(m.config.hidden_size, m.config.num_attention_heads, m.config.kv_dim)"` for both models — are they aligned?

ben: also flagging tokenizer drift — Mixtral tokenizes some prefixes shorter, which changes the acceptance probability calculation for drafts. if the draft thinks a token boundary is at +2 but primary at +1, acceptance tuning becomes noisy. seen this before with family mismatches.

mike: verified dims:
- mixtral: hidden=8192 heads=64 kv_dim=128
- llama-2-13b: hidden=5120 heads=40 kv_dim=128
so kv_dim matches but head count differs. rope_scale was 1.0 on mixtral, 0.5 on llama.

anna: that head mismatch + different RoPE scaling explains a lot. runtime kernel selection checks `heads==kernel_heads && rope_scale==expected` before using the optimized fused-attn kernel. if either fails -> generic attention path (much slower).

ben: tokenizer mismatch + speculative acceptance_rate=0.25 is pretty aggressive for cross-family pairing. i'd try 0.15 or 0.12 first, and increase `timeout_ms` a bit so we avoid extra fallbacks causing hot paths.

infra-bot: deploy: canary bump for mixtral-llama pairing (canary-1769998888) scheduled. traces: https://perf.redwood/traces/1769998888

mike: quick experiment results: acceptance_rate=0.18, force-kernel-pin to fused-attn-for-heads=64 (forced kernel) and set `kv.layout=1` (avoid realloc) -> p95 token latency drops from 210ms -> 190ms (close to baseline). acceptance success down from 78% -> 68%, so more fallbacks to final model (token cost +6% per 1k tokens).

sara: tradeoff expected. we either accept higher token cost or punt on latency. another angle: runtime RoPE rescaling shim — rescale draft/key embeddings so draft logits align with primary. we have a prototype that applies per-head RoPE multiplier at runtime (cheap). worth testing if it recovers acceptance without kernel churn.

anna: implementation note: the shim must be applied before KV-layout canonicalization; otherwise kv bytes differ and we still re-alloc. also watch memory pressure if we rescale in-place.

ben: on batching: continuous batching (windowed) with microbatching of 8 reduced avg latency at low qps but amplified tail because of blocking on kernel selection. switching to adaptive-binning helped in last perf run.

mike: i ran the ROI: after forcing fused kernel + rope shim prototype + acceptance=0.18 -> p95=185ms, acceptance=64%, cost delta +3%. good compromise. need more matrix runs: acceptance in [0.1,0.2,0.25], rope_scale shim [off, 0.8x, 1.0x], kv.layout [auto, 1, pinned].

sara: also add tokenizer normalization test (lowercase/normalize unicode) in the matrix — tokenizer mismatch was the silent killer in previous pairings with Qwen.

anna: can we add a small perf test harness that runs 5k synthetic prompts with realistic prefix diversity and measures: kernel-switches, avg kernel launch ms, kv realloc count, acceptance rate, p50/p95 latency, token cost? put results to the per-route dashboard.

mike: yes i'll provision the job and add to `eng-runtime/perf` dashboard. tagging folks: @sara @ben for config review.

ben: ok i'll own tokenizer normalization and acceptance tuning sweeps. sara you take RoPE shim and kernel-pin fallback logic?

sara: yup i'll pick it up. i'll post a draft PR with microbenchmarks.

deploy-bot: canary finished: 50k requests, regressions flagged: none after kernel-pin + shim in the next run. :white_check_mark:

mike: awesome — follow-ups: (1) perf matrix job, (2) add telemetry for `rope_scale` mismatch events, (3) telemetry for draft vs primary token-length drift. i'll open tickets.

anna: thanks all. short notes: be conservative on acceptance for cross-family pairing; prefer runtime rescale over disabling optimized kernels.

ben: +1 :thumbsup:

mike: thanks. i'll post the perf job id when ready (job-1769999001).
